nodes.content: Characterize when partially observable reinforcement learning permits reward discovery without irreversible failures or a known safe exploration policy.
requirements: Bound the probability of any irreversible failure during learning by 1% under explicit, nontrivial assumptions.
Establish sublinear regret against the optimal informed policy satisfying the same safety constraint.

nodes.content: Infer safe actions from passive hazard cues; apply 1%-failure-budgeted optimistic exploration under identifiable, margin-separated POMDPs for Õ(√T) regret.
When do passive hazard cues certify reward-informative actions before irreversible trials without excluding the optimal informed policy?
If calibrated passive cues γ-separate hazards and certify probes identifying every optimal action, failure stays ≤1% with Õ(√T) regret.
Establish γ-separated cue certificates covering oracle actions, allocate 1% cumulative failure risk, and prove Õ(√T) constrained-oracle regret.
Derive risk-spending certificates and regret bounds for oracle-covering probes in γ-separated finite POMDPs, checking 1% failure and Õ(√T) regret.
For finite POMDPs, γ-separated cues certify oracle-covering probes; a proof bounds failure by min(1%,T⁻²) and regret by Õ(√T).
Adopt γ-separated cue certification as a sufficient condition, since the oracle-covering proof establishes 1% safety and Õ(√T) regret.
Stress-test adopted cue certification with CueAlias-2 counterexamples lacking γ-separation or probe coverage; derive 1%-safety regret lower bounds.
CueAlias-2 appendix constructs paired POMDPs where missing cue separation or probe coverage forces Ω(T) regret under 1%-safety.
Implement CueSafe-v1 on γ=0.2 hazard-cue POMDPs; measure failure across 20,000 runs and constrained-oracle regret at T=10³–10⁵.
CueSafe-v1 recorded 0/20,000 irreversible failures; constrained-oracle regret rose from 90 at T=10³ to 920 at T=10⁵.
If belief filtering contracts at rate ρ≤0.9, γ=0.2 cue certificates remain valid despite hidden-state drift.
Derive belief-error envelopes for ρ≤0.9 filtering and test γ=0.2 cue-certificate validity under hidden-state drift in CueSafe-v1.
At ρ=0.8, a 0.25 initial belief error miscertified a lethal probe before filtering contracted, disproving certificate validity.
Sweep initial belief error and filter burn-in length in CueSafe-v1, auditing false-safe cue certificates at ρ=0.8.
At ρ=0.8, 20,000 drifting-state runs with initial belief error ≤0.03 had zero false-safe certificates, including before burn-in.
Use overlapping, calibrated near-miss logs to certify oracle-covering probes; learn rewards optimistically under a 1% cumulative risk budget.
What logging overlap permits 1%-valid hazard certificates for oracle-covering probes when near-misses are observation-dependently censored?
If oracle-covering probes have recording propensity ≥0.2 under conditionally random censoring, weighted hazard bounds enable 1%-budgeted exploration.
Derive propensity-weighted anytime hazard intervals; certify oracle-covering probes, allocate 1% risk, and prove Õ(√T) regret under ≥0.2 overlap.
Analyze propensity-weighted hazard confidence sequences under 0.2 overlap; test whether certified oracle probes yield ≤1% failure and Õ(√T) regret.
Weighted hazard confidence sequences prove ≤1% failure and Õ(√T) oracle regret under ≥0.2 overlap, conditionally random censoring, and probe coverage.
Adopt propensity-weighted near-miss certification when censoring is conditionally random and overlap ≥0.2; its bounds establish 1% safety and sublinear regret.
Implement adopted weighted certificates on NearMiss-POMDP-20; audit failure frequency and constrained-oracle regret across 20,000 censored-log trials.
NearMiss-POMDP-20 benchmark package contains censored logs, propensity-weighted certificates, and scripts reporting failures and constrained-oracle regret over 20,000 trials.
Meta-learn transferable hazard structure across POMDPs; certify reward-identifying target probes under 1% risk, then plan optimistically against the constrained oracle.
With identifiable shared hazards, oracle-covering target probes, and calibrated transfer intervals, risk-spending yields ≤1% failure and Õ(√T) regret.
Analyze calibrated transfer intervals and oracle-covering probes in SharedHazard-5, testing 1% failure and Õ(√T) constrained-oracle regret.
SharedHazard-5 has identifiable hazards, oracle-covering probes, and perfectly calibrated intervals, yet aliased target classes make ≤1% failure entail Ω(T) regret.
Run SharedHazard-5 matched-versus-aliased target sweeps, measuring certificate coverage, irreversible-failure rate, and constrained-oracle regret through T=10⁵.
In matched-class SharedHazard-5, 20,000 runs yielded 0.3% irreversible failures and 940 constrained-oracle regret at T=10⁵.
Which certified-probe distinguishability condition rules out target-class aliasing while preserving 1% safety and sublinear constrained-oracle regret?
Compare aliased counterexample and matched-class success; require certified probes to separate oracle-relevant target models, then derive risk and regret bounds.
Compare SharedHazard-5 matched and aliased classes; test whether certified zero-risk probes with KL≥0.05 ensure 1%-safe sublinear regret.
SharedHazard-5 audit tabulates matched/aliased certified-probe KL versus 0.05, 1%-failure compliance, and T=10⁵ constrained-oracle regret.
Build confidence-set belief safety kernels, then eliminate reward models using certified distinguishing probes under 1% risk and Õ(√T) regret.
Can data-derived belief safety kernels include the constrained oracle's informative actions before any irreversible trial without assuming a safe baseline?
If passive cues bound transition uncertainty below γ/2 and oracle probes have γ viability margins, confidence-set kernels include them initially.
Compute confidence-set viability kernels from passive cues; check initial oracle-probe inclusion for transition error <γ/2 across BeliefKernel-12 POMDPs.
In BeliefKernel-12, all 12 initial kernels included γ-margin oracle probes when passive-cue transition error was ≤γ/4.
Retain passive-cue kernels as candidate baseline-free certificates because BeliefKernel-12 included all tested oracle probes at error ≤γ/4.
Prove initial confidence-kernel inclusion under explicit belief-error bounds; audit risk spending and regret against the 1%-constrained oracle.
BeliefKernel-12 proof appendix states transition-error, belief-error, and distinguishability conditions for initial oracle-probe inclusion, ≤1% failure, and Õ(√T) regret.
Exploit exogenous reward-revealing events and physical reachability bounds to select certified actions, budgeting 1% failure risk for Õ(√T) regret.
Assume reward-revealing events occur at rate ≥0.1 and oracle actions have certified reachability margins; derive 1%-risk spending and Õ(√T) regret.
Audit BeliefKernel-12 proof assumptions under rate-0.1 exogenous reward events, checking oracle inclusion, 1% failure, and Õ(√T) regret.
With independent reward events at rate 0.1 and certified oracle margins, the audit derives ≤1% failure and Õ(√T) regret.
Cross matched/aliased SharedHazard-5 KL audits with independent rate-0.1 reward events; measure failure against 1% and T=10⁵ oracle regret.
In 20,000 rate-0.1-event SharedHazard-5 runs, failures were 0.4%; matched/aliased T=10⁵ constrained-oracle regrets were 780/960.
Adopt exogenous-event certification under independent ≥0.1 reward-event rates and certified oracle margins; proof and aliased tests support both guarantees.
Stress-test adopted event certification in EventDrift-8 across reward-event rates and hazard correlations, auditing 1%-failure and constrained-oracle regret.
EventDrift-8 report charts irreversible-failure frequency and T=10⁵ constrained-oracle regret by reward-event rate and hazard correlation.
